small_guidance:
- Sweep BLOCK_N in {64, 128, 256, 512} and BLOCK_OC in {16, 32} with num_warps in {4, 8} via `triton.autotune` — current 256×16 with 4 warps may be undersized for the OC=16 case (one OC tile covers all channels, so increasing BLOCK_OC won't help, but a larger BLOCK_N reduces redundant weight loads).
- Pre-load the entire weight tensor (OC=16, IC=3, KD*KH*KW=27 → 1296 floats) into registers/SRAM once per program via a single `tl.load` and reuse across the spatial tile, eliminating the per-(ic,kd,kh,kw) weight reload inside the static loops.
- Try `num_stages=3` and switch the spatial tile to a 2D (oh, ow) layout so the `ih*IW + iw` strides give better L2 reuse across kw within a warp (currently flattened ODHW makes adjacent threads cross row boundaries).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM: tile is (BLOCK_OC × BLOCK_SPATIAL) accumulator, K-loop over IC*KD*KH*KW=81. With OC=16 and K=81, a single program per (N, spatial-tile) can hold the full weight matrix [16,81] in registers and stream input patches — use `tl.dot` on fp32 (or cast to tf32) for the inner GEMM instead of the manual outer-product accumulation.
- Switch input layout to NDHWC (channels-last) so the IC dimension is the contiguous K-axis of the GEMM; this collapses 3 IC loads into one vector load per spatial point and improves coalescing.
- Make the kernel persistent over the batch dimension (N=128 is large) to amortize weight loading: one program processes multiple (n, spatial-tile) pairs reusing the weight tile already resident.
